chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Umar ibn Aban al-Kalbi, who said:

I went to the door of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and al-Mufaddal came out. I faced him and he said, 'What is the matter with you?' I said, 'I intend to do something, but I have not done it until Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) orders me. I intend for Allah to preserve my chastity and lower my gaze while in ihram.' He said, 'As you are,' and entered. He asked him about that, and he said, 'This al-Kalbi is at the door, and he intends to enter ihram and intends to marry, so that Allah will lower his gaze by that. If you order him to do it, he will do it, otherwise he will turn away from that.' He said to me, 'Order him to do it and let him be modest.'

The meaning in this report is one of two things: one is that he ordered him to do that before entering into ihram; as for after the contract of ihram, it is not permissible in any case. The other meaning is that it is to be taken as a form of taqiyya (dissimulation), because that is the view of some of the Sunnis.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: State of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.الْمُفَضَّل: Al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, a companion of the Imams
key_terms.عَقْد: Contract (specifically the formalization of the ritual state)

ai.seo_question: Can a pilgrim marry while in the state of ihram according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Umar ibn Aban al-Kalbi sought Imam al-Sadiq’s permission to marry while in ihram to facilitate lowering his gaze, a specific exception to the general prohibition of marriage during Hajj. The juristic analysis in al-Istibsar clarifies that this ruling likely applied before the formalization of ihram or was based on taqiyya, reflecting the flexibility within Shia fiqh regarding the preservation of chastity during the sacred state.
